# Benchmark baseline of internal/bid on linux/amd64 (targets T1.6.4 and T13).
#
# Taken on a GitHub Actions hosted runner (AMD EPYC 7763, 4 vCPUs) by the
# bench job of go-decimal-proposal's build.yml, run 43038395877 on
# 2026-11-12, at 3ed6f13238 (branch perf/t13-final), with
#   go test -c -o bid.test internal/bid
#   ./bid.test -test.run XXX -test.bench BenchmarkKernel -test.benchmem \
#       -test.count 8 -test.benchtime 100ms
# in the directory src/internal/bid, and the lines below are that output
# unedited (the first line is the runner's CPU, as the job records it).
# The file is in benchstat form; compare a later run with
#   benchstat testdata/bench_baseline_linux_amd64.txt new.txt
#
# Hosted runners differ from run to run (the previous baselines ran on an
# AMD EPYC 7763 at 32c14fd1b1 on 2026-11-01, an AMD EPYC 9V74 at
# f79bf54f87 on 2026-11-09, and an AMD EPYC 9V45 at 7262cd2876 on
# 2026-11-10 and at 1395a73231 on 2026-11-11, the last with the AppendSci
# rows copied from the Append rows, and an AMD EPYC 9V74 at 246d126f18 and
# at db52e6cb46 on 2026-11-11; their figures are in this file's git
# history), so the
# figures indicate the platform's magnitude and
# a run on a different runner is not a like-for-like comparison. That is why
# the band stays at 20% here while darwin/arm64's is 10%.
#
# Rows are Op/Width/Class. Width 64 and 128 are the decimal kernel; float64 is
# the reference row, where the language has a counterpart. Every row includes
# the benchmark loop floor (the float64 add row is nearly all floor).
#
# The ratchet is TestBenchRatchet, opt-in:
#   go test -run TestBenchRatchet internal/bid -args -bid.ratchet
# It measures each row in short runs and takes the smallest time, as it does
# for the samples below. A row fails when its time is over
#   baseline * (1 + ratchet-band) + ratchet-slack-ns
# or when it allocates. The slack stands for the timer resolution on rows of
# about a nanosecond. The baseline moves only by a deliberate commit that
# replaces this file.
#
# ratchet-band: 0.20
# ratchet-slack-ns: 0.5
# AppendSci/64 and AppendSci/128 (added 2026-11-11): the samples of the Append rows
# above, copied, NOT a runner measurement; the next bench run replaces them.
